batchName: Empire: From Constantine's Sons to Theodosius (AD 337-395) - Medium Batch 2
chapterName: Empire: From Constantine's Sons to Theodosius (AD 337-395)

questions.question: Why were Julian and his half-brother probably spared in the family massacre of 337?
options: They were hidden by a bishop
questions.explanation: The two boys were probably spared because of their youth; Julian was about six. His father was among those killed.
questions.sourceQuote: They were probably spared because they were so young.

questions.question: What do modern historians stress about the Edict of Thessalonica?
options: It was issued by the Pope
It applied only to the western empire
It was aimed only at Constantinople
questions.explanation: Modern historians stress that the edict targeted Constantinople and did not make Christianity the state religion. It defined who could call themselves "catholic".
questions.sourceQuote: Modern historians stress that the edict was aimed only at Constantinople and did not make Christianity the state religion.

questions.question: What satire did Julian write in reply to the people of Antioch mocking his philosopher's beard?
questions.explanation: After the Antiochenes mocked his beard, Julian answered with the satire "Beard Hater". His stay in the city lasted a prickly nine months.
questions.sourceQuote: After a prickly nine-month stay in Antioch, the great city of Roman Syria, where citizens mocked his philosopher's beard and he answered with a satire called the "Beard Hater", Julian set out against Persia in March AD 363.

questions.question: A rival philosopher whom Julian took as mentor supposedly made a statue of which goddess smile and laugh?
questions.explanation: The philosopher practised theurgy, magic meant to call down the gods, and supposedly animated a statue of Hecate. A teacher warned Julian off him, but Julian sought him out anyway.
questions.sourceQuote: One teacher warned him about a rival philosopher who practised theurgy, magical rituals meant to call down the gods, and who had supposedly made a statue of the goddess Hecate smile and laugh.

questions.question: Why did Valens' scouts badly underestimate the Gothic army before Adrianople?
options: The Goths hid in a forest
The Huns arrived later as allies
questions.explanation: The scouts counted about 10,000 Goths but missed the cavalry, who were away gathering food. When that cavalry returned, it surrounded the Romans.
questions.sourceQuote: His scouts counted about 10,000 Goths, missing the cavalry who were away gathering food.

questions.question: After his year of detention, who spoke up for Julian so he could go to study in Athens?
questions.explanation: The empress interceded and Julian was allowed to study in Athens. There he was initiated into the Eleusinian Mysteries.
questions.sourceQuote: After his year of detention, the empress spoke up for him and he was allowed to study in Athens.

questions.question: Under Theodosius' treaty of 382, what were the Goths allowed to do?
options: Join Roman legions as ordinary recruits
Pay tribute in exchange for land in Asia
Take over the province of Gaul
Return north of the Danube in peace
Settle south of the Danube under their own leaders
questions.explanation: The Goths settled south of the Danube under their own leaders and fought for Rome as a separate force. It brought peace but created a semi-independent people inside the empire.
questions.sourceQuote: A treaty of 3 October 382 let them settle south of the Danube under their own leaders, fighting for Rome as a separate force.

questions.question: What role did Constantius II originally intend Julian to play in Gaul?
options: A hostage held by the army
questions.explanation: Julian was meant to be a figurehead while experienced officials governed. Instead the bookish young man taught himself to command an army.
questions.sourceQuote: The idea was that Julian would be a figurehead while experienced officials ran things.

questions.question: What did Julian do after his generals advised against besieging Ctesiphon?
options: Burned his fleet and pushed inland
questions.explanation: Julian burned his fleet and marched inland, a fatal mistake. The Persians burned crops ahead of him and flooded the land behind, forcing a retreat.
questions.sourceQuote: His generals advised against a siege, so Julian burned his fleet and pushed inland.

questions.question: Of 43 temple destructions reported in written sources, how many have archaeologists confirmed?
questions.explanation: Archaeologists have confirmed only four of the 43 reported destructions. Modern historians doubt the claim that Theodosius crushed paganism.
questions.sourceQuote: Of 43 temple destructions reported in written sources, archaeologists have confirmed only four.
